input.command:
cd /private/var/folders/kp/vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn/T/barcode-iw4qd_ox; cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-var-folders-kp-vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn-T-barcode-iw4qd-ox/d8781892-a662-4e96-954a-d6a46648a7bf/scratchpad/c.py <<'EOF'
import numpy as np,subprocess
from PIL import Image
b=np.array(Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')).astype(float)[100]
N=b.shape[0]
for L in 'ABCDEFGHIJ':
    out=subprocess.run(['ffmpeg','-loglevel','error','-i',f'videos/{L}.mp4','-vf','scale=1:1,fps=2','-f','rawvideo','-pix_fmt','rgb24','-'],capture_output=True).stdout
    a=np.frombuffer(out,np.uint8).reshape(-1,3).astype(float)
    idx=np.linspace(0,len(a)-1,N).astype(int)
    print(L,len(a),np.abs(a[idx]-b).mean())
EOF

I sampled each of the ten candidate videos at 2 frames per second, shrank every frame to its average color, and stretched each sequence to the barcode's width. Then I measured how far each video's colors were from the barcode's (mean difference per color channel, on a 0–255 scale; lower is a closer match).

| Option | Video | Difference |
|---|---|---|
| **B** | **J Balvin – Ay Vamos** | **24.8** |
| F | MC Fioti – Bum Bum Tam Tam | 54.8 |
| D | Natti Natasha x Ozuna – Criminal | 57.3 |
| J | Maluma – Felices los 4 | 57.3 |
| A | Pedro Capó & Farruko – Calma (Remix) | 59.6 |
| I | Shakira ft. Maluma – Chantaje | 60.8 |
| E | Shakira – Waka Waka | 62.5 |
| G | Becky G ft. Bad Bunny – Mayores | 64.3 |
| H | J Balvin & Willy William – Mi Gente | 65.5 |
| C | DJ Snake et al. – Taki Taki | 68.6 |

"Ay Vamos" matches far better than any other option: its difference is less than half that of the next-best video. I didn't visually check individual frames, but a gap this large is a strong signal.

Answer: B
